claim: Ascorbate (vitamin C) is an essential micronutrient in humans.
source: Ascorbate (vitamin C) is an essential micronutrient in humans.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about vitamin C being essential for humans.

claim: Severe chronic deficiency of ascorbate, termed scurvy, has been associated with increased susceptibility to infections.
source: The severe chronic deficiency of ascorbate, termed scurvy, has long been associated with increased susceptibility to infections.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about scurvy and infection susceptibility.

claim: Ascorbate is a potent enhancer for antibody response by facilitating IL-21/STAT3-dependent plasma cell differentiation in mouse and human B cells.
source: From a micronutrient analysis, we identified ascorbate as a potent enhancer for antibody response by facilitating the IL-21/STAT3-dependent plasma cell differentiation in mouse and human B cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the micronutrient analysis described in the manuscript.

claim: The effect of ascorbate is unique as other antioxidants failed to promote plasma cell differentiation.
source: The effect of ascorbate is unique as other antioxidants failed to promote plasma cell differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing ascorbate to other antioxidants.

claim: Ascorbate is critical during early B cell activation by poising the cells to plasma cell lineage without affecting the proximal IL-21/STAT3 signaling and the overall transcriptome.
source: Ascorbate is especially critical during early B cell activation by poising the cells to plasma cell lineage without affecting the proximal IL-21/STAT3 signaling and the overall transcriptome.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing timing of VC effect and lack of changes in signaling and transcriptome.

claim: Ascorbate facilitates TET2/3-mediated DNA modification and demethylation of multiple elements at the Prdm1 locus.
source: As a cofactor for epigenetic enzymes, ascorbate facilitates TET2/3-mediated DNA modification and demethylation of multiple elements at the Prdm1 locus.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from 5hmC profiling and DNA methylation analysis.

claim: DNA demethylation augments STAT3 association at the Prdm1 promoter and a downstream enhancer, ensuring efficient gene expression and plasma cell differentiation.
source: DNA demethylation augments STAT3 association at the Prdm1 promoter and a downstream enhancer, thus ensuring efficient gene expression and plasma cell differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data showing increased STAT3 binding after VC treatment.

claim: An adequate level of ascorbate is required for antibody response.
source: The results suggest that an adequate level of ascorbate is required for antibody response and highlight how micronutrients may regulate the activity of epigenetic enzymes to regulate gene expression.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing VC's effect on plasma cell differentiation and antibody secretion.

claim: Epigenetic enzymes can function as sensors to gauge the availability of metabolites and influence cell fate decisions.
source: Our findings imply that epigenetic enzymes can function as sensors to gauge the availability of metabolites and influence cell fate decisions.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Humans are unable to synthesize ascorbate due to a mutation in GULO (L-gulono-gamma-lactone oxidase).
source: Due to a mutation in GULO (L-gulono-gamma-lactone oxidase), humans are unable to synthesize ascorbate and depend on dietary sources to achieve VC adequacy (Nishikimi et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Overt VC deficiency and suboptimal VC status occurs in ~7.1% and ~25% of adults in the US respectively.
source: Although scurvy is rare nowadays, national surveillance data indicate that overt VC deficiency and suboptimal VC status occurs in ~7.1% and ~25% of adults in the US respectively (Schleicher et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to surveillance data.

claim: VC insufficiency is more prevalent in some subgroups, including the elderly, smokers, those with limited dietary intake, and those with increased oxidative stress due to illnesses.
source: VC insufficiency is even more prevalent in some subgroups, including the elderly, smokers, those with limited dietary intake, and those with increased oxidative stress due to illnesses (Isola et al., 2019; Cahill and El-Sohemy, 2010; Lima de Araújo et al., 2012; Na et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Excess oral supplementation does not increase the steady-state VC concentration beyond the physiological level maintained by absorption and excretion.
source: Notably, excess oral supplementation does not increase the steady-state VC concentration beyond the physiological level maintained by absorption and excretion (Padayatty et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: VC deficiency impairs the immune response to influenza infection in Gulo-knockout mice.
source: For instance, using Gulo-knockout mice that are unable to synthesize VC, studies have shown that VC deficiency impairs the immune response to influenza infection.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies using Gulo-knockout mice.

claim: Influenza infection in Gulo-deficient mice increased the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β) and promoted lung pathology without affecting viral clearance.
source: One study showed that influenza infection in these mice increased the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β) and promoted lung pathology without affecting viral clearance (Li et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a specific study.

claim: Gulo-deficient mice are defective in viral clearance due to decreased type I interferon response.
source: Another study showed that Gulo-deficient mice are defective in viral clearance due to decreased type I interferon response (Kim et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a specific study.

claim: VC is important for T-cell-dependent antibody response after immunization in guinea pigs.
source: In addition to Gulo-deficient mice, guinea pigs are naturally unable to synthesize VC and have been used as a model to show that VC is important for T-cell-dependent antibody response after immunization (Prinz et al., 1980; Feigen et al., 1982).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies in guinea pigs.

claim: VC is a cofactor for several epigenetic enzymes, including ten-eleven-translocation (TET).
source: In addition to its antioxidative function, VC is a cofactor for several epigenetic enzymes, including ten-eleven-translocation (TET; Blaschke et al., 2013; Minor et al., 2013; He et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: TET proteins (TET1, TET2, TET3) are critical for DNA demethylation by oxidizing 5-methylcytosine (5mC) into 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) and other minor oxidized bases.
source: TET proteins (TET1, TET2, TET3) are critical for DNA demethylation by oxidizing 5-methylcytosine (5mC) into 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) and other minor oxidized bases, which are the intermediates for demethylation (Lio and Rao, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: VC enhances neuronal and hematological differentiations in vitro.
source: Besides enhancing neuronal and hematological differentiations in vitro (Wu and Zhang, 2017), VC facilitates the differentiation of induced regulatory T cells by potentiating TET-mediated demethylation of the Foxp3 intronic enhancer CNS2 (Sasidharan Nair et al., 2016; Yue and Rao, 2020; Someya et al., 2017; Yue et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: VC facilitates the differentiation of induced regulatory T cells by potentiating TET-mediated demethylation of the Foxp3 intronic enhancer CNS2.
source: Besides enhancing neuronal and hematological differentiations in vitro (Wu and Zhang, 2017), VC facilitates the differentiation of induced regulatory T cells by potentiating TET-mediated demethylation of the Foxp3 intronic enhancer CNS2 (Sasidharan Nair et al., 2016; Yue and Rao, 2020; Someya et al., 2017; Yue et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Plasma cells express the key transcription factor BLIMP1 (encoded by Prdm1).
source: Plasma cells express the key transcription factor (TF) BLIMP1 (encoded by Prdm1) and can be induced by T-cell-derived signals, including CD40 ligand and IL-21.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about plasma cells.

claim: Plasma cells can be induced by T-cell-derived signals, including CD40 ligand and IL-21.
source: Plasma cells express the key transcription factor (TF) BLIMP1 (encoded by Prdm1) and can be induced by T-cell-derived signals, including CD40 ligand and IL-21.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about plasma cell induction.

claim: Using a two-step in vitro system, only around 20% plasma cells were generated after 7 days without VC supplementation.
source: However, using this two-step culture, only around 20% plasma cells were generated after 7 days (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The combination of B27 and VC significantly increased the percentage of plasma cells by at least threefold after 7-day culture.
source: In our B cell culture system, the combination of B27 and VC significantly increased the percentage of plasma cells by at least threefold after the 7-day culture (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1C and D.

claim: VC was the major component responsible for the enhancement of plasma cell differentiation.
source: Remarkably, VC was the major component responsible for the enhancement of plasma cell differentiation (Figure 1C and D), while B27 alone or B27 without antioxidants (B27-AO) had no effect.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1C and D.

claim: Culture supplements and VC had no significant effect on cell numbers and cell death.
source: These culture supplements and VC had no significant effect on cell numbers and cell death (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C), suggesting that the increased plasma cells were not due to the preferential increased in survival.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C.

claim: NAC had no significant effect on plasma cell differentiation.
source: To address this possibility, we cultured B cells in the presence of another antioxidant N-acetylcysteine (NAC). Unlike VC, NAC had no significant effect on plasma cell differentiation (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1C and D.

claim: The structurally similar stereoisomer erythorbic acid (EA) could similarly promote plasma cell differentiation.
source: The specific activity of VC likely requires an enediol group as the structurally similar stereoisomer erythorbic acid (EA) could similarly promote plasma cell differentiation (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The depletion of VC with ascorbate oxidase abolished the plasma-cell-enhancing activity.
source: Importantly, the depletion of VC with ascorbate oxidase abolished the plasma-cell-enhancing activity (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Mock and VC-treated cells had low oxidative levels.
source: The data showed that the mock and VC-treated cells similarly had low oxidative levels (Figure 1E, left panel), which is supported by the fact that the addition of NAC during the CellROX assay did not significantly decrease the fluorescent signal (Figure 1E, second panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The activated B cells in the culture system exhibited low oxidative stress.
source: The results demonstrated that the activated B cells in our system exhibited low oxidative stress.
evidence: This is inferred from the CellROX assay data.

claim: The effect of VC on plasma cells is independent of its well-established general antioxidative function.
source: Thus, the effect of VC on plasma cells is independent of its well-established general antioxidative function.
evidence: This is inferred from the low oxidative stress in cultured cells and lack of effect of other antioxidants.

claim: VC treatment increased the percentage of plasma cells and the levels of secreted IgG2c and IgG3 in B cells stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and LPS with IFN-γ.
source: VC treatment increased the percentage of plasma cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A) and the levels of secreted IgG2c and IgG3 in B cells stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and LPS with IFN-γ (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4A and B.

claim: VC increases the secretion of IgG1 in B cells stimulated with LPS and IL-4.
source: Consistent with the 40LB system, VC also increases the secretion of IgG1 in B cells stimulated with LPS and IL-4 (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4B.

claim: VC promotes plasma cell differentiation and antibody secretion in various stimulated conditions independent of isotypes.
source: Together, these results suggested that VC promotes plasma cell differentiation and antibody secretion in various stimulated conditions independent of isotypes.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing VC effects across different stimulation conditions and antibody isotypes.

claim: VC facilitated the differentiation of human antibody-secreting cells in both anti-CD40/CpG/IL-21 and SAC/IL-21 conditions.
source: Consistent with its effect on mouse cells, VC facilitated the differentiation of human antibody-secreting cells in both conditions (Figure 1F and G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1F and G.

claim: VC increased the percentage of antibody-secreting cells (IgDloCD38hi) and early plasma cells (CD27hiCD38hi) in human B cells using a two-step system.
source: Under this condition, VC increased the percentage of antibody-secreting cells (IgDloCD38hi) and early plasma cells (CD27hiCD38hi; Figure 1—figure supplement 5B and C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5B and C.

claim: The antibody-secreting cells cultured with VC downregulated the surface expression of CD19.
source: The antibody-secreting cells cultured with VC downregulated the surface expression of CD19, a characteristic of mature plasma cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 5B and C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5B and C.

claim: VC has similar effect on B cells isolated from WT and IgHCGG mice.
source: The data showed that VC has similar effect on the B cells isolated from WT and IgHCGG mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), suggesting that the plasma cells generated in the VC culture are mostly derived from naïve B cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The percentage of BLIMP1- and IRF4-positive cells increased substantially after 7-day culture with VC.
source: Consistent with CD138, the percentage of BLIMP1- and IRF4-positive cells increased substantially after 7-day culture with VC (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2A and B.

claim: VC-treated B cells downregulated the B-lineage TF PAX5.
source: Similar to mature plasma cells, VC-treated B cells also downregulated the B-lineage TF PAX5 (Figure 2A, upper panel, and B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2A and B.

claim: B cells secreted minimal number of antibodies after the first-step culture regardless of VC.
source: While B cells secreted minimal number of antibodies after the first-step culture regardless of VC (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), VC treatment significantly enhanced the antibody secretion after IL-21 stimulation during the second-step culture (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and Figure 2C.

claim: VC treatment significantly enhanced antibody secretion after IL-21 stimulation during the second-step culture.
source: While B cells secreted minimal number of antibodies after the first-step culture regardless of VC (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), VC treatment significantly enhanced the antibody secretion after IL-21 stimulation during the second-step culture (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The VC treatment group had a significantly higher proportion (~84%) of plasma cells compared to control (~35%) in an extended culture.
source: The effect of VC was not simply due to accelerating the kinetics of plasma cell differentiation as the VC treatment group still had a significantly higher proportion (~84%) of plasma cells compared to control (~35%) in an extended culture of B cells with 40LB (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B.

claim: VC-treated B cells significantly downregulated CD19 similar to mature plasma cells.
source: Similar to mature plasma cells, the VC-treated B cells significantly downregulated CD19 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3C.

claim: The addition of VC during the first step is sufficient to enhance plasma cell differentiation.
source: The data showed that the addition of VC during the first step is sufficient to enhance plasma cell differentiation (Figure 3AII), while the effect is less pronounced when VC is added during the second step (Figure 3AIII).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: VC is important for conditioning the B cells during the initial activation period.
source: These data demonstrated that VC is important for conditioning the B cells during the initial activation period.
evidence: This is inferred from the timing experiments showing VC is most effective during the first step.

claim: B cells were similar in function and phenotype after the initial 4 days of culture regardless of VC treatment.
source: B cells were similar in function and phenotype after the initial 4 days of culture regardless of VC treatment (Figure 3B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: VC significantly enhanced plasma cell differentiation regardless of 40LB cells during the second step.
source: The results show that VC significantly enhanced plasma cell differentiation regardless of 40LB cells by measuring CD138 (Figure 3D and E), antibody secretion (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), and TF expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3D, E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: Stimulation with IL-21 for 24 hr was sufficient to induce significantly more plasma cells from the VC-treated B cells.
source: While the percentage of plasma cells was similarly low in mock- and VC-treated cells after first-step culture (Figure 3B), stimulation with IL-21 for 24 hr was sufficient to induce significantly more plasma cells from the VC-treated B cells (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3B and 3F.

claim: VC conditions B cells to be responsive to the IL-21-induced plasma cell differentiation.
source: These results suggest that VC conditions B cells to be responsive to the IL-21-induced plasma cell differentiation.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing VC-treated cells respond better to IL-21.

claim: IL-21R expression was comparable between mock- and VC-treated cells.
source: The data showed that IL-21R expression was comparable between mock- and VC-treated cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: VC has no significant effect on STAT3 phosphorylation in response to IL-21.
source: The results showed that VC has no significant effect on the STAT3 phosphorylation in response to IL-21 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: VC-mediated conditioning of B cells is not due to a heightened IL-21 proximal signaling.
source: These data suggest that VC-mediated conditioning of the B cells is not due to a heightened IL-21 proximal signaling.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of effect on IL-21R expression and STAT3 phosphorylation.

claim: B cell activation induced substantial changes in transcriptomes, with thousands of differentially expressed genes.
source: As expected, B cell activation induced substantial changes in transcriptomes, with thousands of differentially expressed genes (DEGs; Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figures 5A and B.

claim: The transcriptomes of B cells are highly similar between control and VC-treated cells, with only one and five genes differentially decreased and increased, respectively.
source: Surprisingly, the transcriptomes of B cells are highly similar between control and VC-treated cells (Figure 5C), with only one and five genes differentially decreased and increased, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The majority of differentially expressed genes between mock and VC-treated cells are non-coding transcripts and proteins with unknown function.
source: Among the DEGs, the majority of them are non-coding transcripts (e.g., Gm48840, Gm13192, Gm5340) and proteins with unknown function (1700120K04Rik, Lrp2bp).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the RNA-seq data.

claim: The effect of VC on plasma cell differentiation dramatically decreased in the absence of TET2 and TET3.
source: Remarkably, the effect of VC on plasma cell differentiation dramatically decreased in the absence of TET2 and TET3 as measured by percentages of CD138+ (Figure 6E and G) or BLIMP1+ (Figure 6F and H) B cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6E, F, G, and H.

claim: The ability of VC to enhance plasma cell differentiation is via TET2 and TET3.
source: Therefore, these results strongly suggested that the ability of VC to enhance plasma cell differentiation is via TET2 and TET3.
evidence: This is inferred from the loss of VC effect in TET2/3 double knockout cells.

claim: The addition of VC significantly increased the amount of 5hmC compared to mock control B cells at both day 4 and day 7.
source: The addition of VC significantly increased the amount of 5hmC compared to those in the mock control B cells at both time points (Figure 7A; compare mock and VC), validating that VC enhances TET activity in B cells.
evidence: This is supported by DNA dot blot data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: VC enhances TET activity in B cells.
source: The addition of VC significantly increased the amount of 5hmC compared to those in the mock control B cells at both time points (Figure 7A; compare mock and VC), validating that VC enhances TET activity in B cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the increased 5hmC levels after VC treatment.

claim: Naïve B cells had the highest density of 5hmC compared with B cells from day 4 or day 7 culture.
source: Naïve B cells had the highest density of 5hmC compared with B cells from day 4 or day 7 culture (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by DNA dot blot data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The decreased 5hmC is consistent with the passive dilution of 5hmC after cell divisions.
source: The decreased 5hmC is consistent with the passive dilution of 5hmC after cell divisions as the 5hmC modification pattern is not replicated on the newly synthesized DNA (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is inferred from the mechanism of 5hmC replication and supported by the schematic in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: The number of 5hmC-enriched regions correlated with the levels of 5hmC.
source: Overall, the number of 5hmC-enriched regions correlated with the levels of 5hmC (Figure 7A): naïve B cells contained the most 5hmC-enriched regions; B cells activated for 4 days (MockDay4) had the lowest; B cells cultured with VC (VCDay4) had significantly more 5hmC-enriched regions compared to mock control (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by 5hmC profiling data shown in Figures 7A and 7B.

claim: B cells cultured for 4 days without VC (MockDay4) lost the majority (87.6%) of the 5hmC-enriched regions that were identified in naïve B cells.
source: Analysis of the differentially hydroxymethylated regions (DhmRs) revealed that B cells cultured for 4 days without VC (MockDay4) lost the majority (87.6%; Figure 7C, left panel, and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A) of the 5hmC-enriched regions that were identified in naïve B cells.
evidence: This is supported by 5hmC profiling data shown in Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A.

claim: VC induced a significant number of 5hmC-enriched regions (72.3%).
source: The analysis of DhmRs revealed that VC induced a significant number of 5hmC-enriched regions (72.3%; Figure 7C, right panel, and Figure 7D), while a small number of regions have decreased 5hmC (3.7%), which may represent the regions undergo demethylation.
evidence: This is supported by 5hmC profiling data shown in Figure 7C and 7D.

claim: Most 5hmC-enriched regions were distal to the transcription start sites.
source: Most of these 5hmC-enriched regions were distal to the transcription start sites (Figure 7—figure supplement 2C–E), suggesting that many of these regions might be potentially regulatory elements as previously described (Lio et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by distance analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2C–E.

claim: VC demonstrated that VC enhanced the enzymatic activity of TET, resulting in a substantial increase in 5hmC throughout the genome.
source: Altogether, the data demonstrated that VC enhanced the enzymatic activity of TET, resulting in a substantial increase in 5hmC throughout the genome.
evidence: This is inferred from the genome-wide 5hmC profiling data.

claim: In naïve B cells, the Prdm1 gene body and several downstream regions are enriched in 5hmC.
source: In naïve B cells, the Prdm1 gene body and several downstream regions are enriched in 5hmC (Figure 8A, top track 'naïve').
evidence: This is supported by 5hmC profiling data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: VC induced the enrichment of 5hmC in at least 14 locations at the Prdm1 locus.
source: VC induced the enrichment of 5hmC in at least 14 locations (teal bars in Figure 8B, MockDay4 vs. VCDay4).
evidence: This is supported by 5hmC profiling data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: E58 is a previously undescribed element located at +58 kb relative to the start of Prdm1.
source: One of the most pronounced enrichment was at E58, a previously undescribed element located at +58 kb relative to the start of Prdm1 (Kwon et al., 2009).
evidence: This is based on the 5hmC profiling data and comparison to previous literature.

claim: Both E27 and E58 are methylated in naïve B cells and are at the center or the edge of demethylating regions, respectively.
source: Overlaying a previously published DNA methylation data demonstrated that both E27 and E58 are methylated in naïve B cells and are at the center or the edge of demethylating regions, respectively (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is supported by overlaying published DNA methylation data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The boundaries between methylated and demethylation regions are enriched in 5hmC.
source: This observation is consistent with a previous notion that the boundaries between methylated and demethylation regions are enriched in 5hmC (Han et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: VC strongly increased STAT3 association at the promoter and E27 in response to IL-21.
source: Strikingly, compared to Mock control, VC strongly increased STAT3 association at the promoter and E27 in response to IL-21 (Figure 8D, bottom two tracks).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: VC and TET are critical regulators of STAT3 association at E27.
source: The results show that VC and TET are critical regulators of STAT3 association at E27, in which the STAT3 binding site is essential for IL-21-induced Prdm1 expression (Kwon et al., 2009).
evidence: This is inferred from the ChIP-seq data and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: STAT3 does not associate with E58 in B cells.
source: Interestingly, while STAT3 does not associate with E58 in B cells, the analysis of previously published ChIP-seq (Kwon et al., 2009) showed that STAT3 could bind to E58 in T cells (Figure 8—figure supplement 1; bottom two tracks).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: STAT3 could bind to E58 in T cells.
source: Interestingly, while STAT3 does not associate with E58 in B cells, the analysis of previously published ChIP-seq (Kwon et al., 2009) showed that STAT3 could bind to E58 in T cells (Figure 8—figure supplement 1; bottom two tracks).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of published ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: A stretch of CpGs at E27 (differentially methylated region [DMR]) was hypomethylated in response to VC compared to mock control.
source: We found that in response to VC a stretch of CpGs at E27 (differentially methylated region [DMR]) was hypomethylated compared to mock control (Figure 9A, Figure 9—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 9A and Figure 9—figure supplement 1A.

claim: E27 DMR remained methylated after VC treatment in the absence of TET2 and TET3.
source: Consistent with our hypothesis, E27 DMR remained methylated after VC treatment in the absence of TET2 and TET3 (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: E58 remained mostly methylated despite enrichment in 5hmC after VC treatment.
source: Interestingly, E58 remained mostly methylated (5mC + 5hmC; Figure 9—figure supplement 1B) despite enrichment in 5hmC after VC treatment (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1B and 5hmC data in Figure 8A.

claim: The CpGs at Prdm1 promoter were mostly demethylated even in the absence of TET2/3.
source: In contrast to E27 and E58, the CpGs at Prdm1 promoter were mostly demethylated even in the absence of TET2/3 (Figure 9—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that the inability to upregulate Prdm1 is not due to promoter hypermethylation in the absence of VC or TET enzymes.
evidence: This is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1C.

claim: VC strongly increased STAT3 binding to E27 in B cells stimulated with IL-21.
source: VC strongly increased STAT3 binding to E27 in B cells stimulated with IL-21 (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 9C.

claim: STAT3 binding to E27 dramatically diminished in the absence of TET2/3.
source: However, the binding dramatically diminished in the absence of TET2/3 (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 9C.

claim: VC facilitates plasma cell differentiation via TET-mediated demethylation of E27, which then becomes permissive to the binding of STAT3 and augments Prdm1 transcription.
source: The data strongly suggest that VC facilitates plasma cell differentiation via TET-mediated demethylation of E27, which then becomes permissive to the binding of STAT3 and augments Prdm1 transcription.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data on DNA methylation, 5hmC, and STAT3 binding.

claim: Plasma cell differentiation is sensitive to the level of VC.
source: In conclusion, our data showed that plasma cell differentiation is sensitive to the level of VC, which can affect the epigenome by modulating the activity of epigenetic enzymes including TET.
evidence: This is inferred from all the experimental data showing VC effects on plasma cell differentiation.

claim: Heightened TET activity may increase the probability of DNA modification/demethylation at critical regulatory elements and may skew the lineage decision of differentiating B cells.
source: Heightened TET activity may increase the probability of the DNA modification/demethylation at critical regulatory elements and may skew the lineage decision of the differentiating B cells (Figure 10).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings, illustrated in Figure 10.

claim: VC supplementation does not prevent 'common cold'.
source: While VC supplementation does not prevent 'common cold,' a comprehensive meta-analysis of 29 clinical trials showed that VC supplementation is associated with shortened duration of symptoms (Hemilä and Chalker, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a meta-analysis.

claim: VC supplementation is associated with shortened duration of common cold symptoms.
source: While VC supplementation does not prevent 'common cold,' a comprehensive meta-analysis of 29 clinical trials showed that VC supplementation is associated with shortened duration of symptoms (Hemilä and Chalker, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a meta-analysis.

claim: Early IgM produced by antibody-secreting cells is important in controlling infection.
source: Giving the importance of early IgM produced by antibody-secreting cells in controlling infection (Nguyen et al., 2017), it is possible that VC deficiency may delay the plasma cell differentiation to result in inferior control of the viruses at the early phase.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: VC deficiency may delay plasma cell differentiation resulting in inferior control of viruses at the early phase.
source: Giving the importance of early IgM produced by antibody-secreting cells in controlling infection (Nguyen et al., 2017), it is possible that VC deficiency may delay the plasma cell differentiation to result in inferior control of the viruses at the early phase.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the experimental findings and cited literature.

claim: VC stabilizes in vitro-induced regulatory T cells by TET-mediated DNA demethylation at the intronic enhancer of Foxp3.
source: For instance, VC stabilizes the in vitro-induced regulatory T cells by TET-mediated DNA demethylation at the intronic enhancer of the key TF Foxp3 (Sasidharan Nair et al., 2016; Someya et al., 2017; Yue et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: αKG modulates macrophage function by facilitating histone demethylation.
source: Another example is αKG, an intermediate in the Kreb cycle and a substrate for many epigenetic enzymes. Studies have shown that αKG modulates macrophage function by facilitating histone demethylation (Liu et al., 2017) and promoting IL-2-sensitive gene expression in T cells by TET-mediated DNA demethylation (Yue et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: αKG promotes IL-2-sensitive gene expression in T cells by TET-mediated DNA demethylation.
source: Another example is αKG, an intermediate in the Kreb cycle and a substrate for many epigenetic enzymes. claim: Epigenetic enzymes may act as rheostats to control appropriate gene transcription by integrating the availability of micronutrients or metabolites.
source: Based on these observations, we hypothesize that epigenetic enzymes may act as rheostats to control appropriate gene transcription by integrating the availability of micronutrients or metabolites.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental findings and literature.

claim: Differentiation from naïve B cells to plasma cells and memory B cells is accompanied by remodeling of the methylome, with more regions being hypomethylated.
source: Studies have shown that differentiation from naïve B cells to plasma cells and memory B cells is accompanied by remodeling of the methylome, with more regions being hypomethylated that is consistent with the role of TET enzymes in cell differentiations (Kulis et al., 2015; Oakes et al., 2016; Lai et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Human memory B cells require a lower level of STAT3 to differentiate into plasma cells compared to naïve B cells.
source: Interestingly, a previous report showed that human memory B cells, compared to naïve B cells, require a lower level of STAT3 to differentiate into plasma cells (Deenick et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: DNA hypomethylation may enhance STAT3 binding.
source: As DNA hypomethylation may enhance STAT3 binding, DNA demethylation may contribute to the lower requirement for STAT3 in memory B cells.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the experimental findings.

claim: The differentiation of plasma cells from naïve B cells may be preferentially affected by VC deficiency.
source: In addition, given the lower methylation levels in memory compared to naïve B cells, we hypothesize that the differentiation of plasma cells from naïve B cells may be preferentially affected by VC deficiency.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental findings and reasoning about methylation differences.
